# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Mute. My inventory: I hold the manual (a table: display value × light color → wire color to cut), I can hear, and my only outgoing channel is gestures, which only Deaf can see. The Blind cannot perceive anything I can send, so I am purely a relay endpoint: Deaf must look at the bomb and speak the display number and light color to me, I look up the answer, and I gesture it back to Deaf, who speaks it to the Blind.

This round I go first with no information received yet. Deaf speaks after me and can't hear anything I'd ever say — and my gestures arrive with no explanation attached. So the job right now is not to transmit data (I have none) but to open the channel and get Deaf talking, since their voice is the one line I can receive and the one line that reaches the Blind. I'll send a clear attention-getting pair — a wave and a "please" — plus a thumbs-up/thumbs-down pair to seed a yes/no control vocabulary we'll need to agree on a color code. Next round, once Deaf speaks, I'll hear their guess at what these mean, confirm or correct, and then teach the seven answer colors one by one with yes/no anchoring.

I must keep every exchanged code gesture-free when Deaf speaks to me — I hear words but only get blanks for embedded gestures, and I can't see anything at all.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🙏", "👍", "👎"])
```

Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Both of you can hear me, but I cannot hear you at all, so answers must come to me only as hand gestures, which I can see. Everything I see on the bomb: a display showing the number 1. A light shining green. Seven wires in a row, numbered 1 to 7 from top to bottom: wire 1 red, wire 2 white, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 orange, wire 5 green, wire 6 purple, wire 7 blue. No labels, no buttons, nothing else printed anywhere. Mute, your four gestures reached me and I read them as hello, please, yes, no. If that is right, adopt this code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, folded hands means I have a question or I need more information, the OK sign means understood or go ahead, and a number is sent as that many fist punches, so three punches means 3. Answer next round with three signs in a row, one per question. Question 1: does the manual cover a bomb with a display, a light and seven wires? Question 2: do any instructions depend on the number shown on the display? Question 3: do any instructions depend on the colour of the light? Blind, you hear me and you can touch the bomb, but do not cut or press anything yet, one wrong action kills all three of us. Report to Mute by voice whatever you feel: batteries, buttons, labels, textures. You can also use the same gesture code toward me: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, fist punches for numbers. Mute, relay anything Blind tells you to me in our code. Nobody acts until the manual rule for this bomb is clear to me and confirmed.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👋 👌]

Deaf has read the bomb aloud: display 1, light green, seven wires in distinct colours, and wire 5 (counting top to bottom) is the only green one. My manual covers exactly this shape — a display row, a light column, outputting the colour of the wire to cut. So I can already solve it: row display=1, column green gives green, which is wire 5. Answering their three questions: yes, the manual covers a display/light/wire bomb (that is all it covers); yes, the display number is the row key; yes, the light colour is the column key — meaning the rule depends on *both*, so both must be re-checked at the moment of cutting. Deaf also gestured [👍 👋 👌], which I take as confirmation of my opening code; their proposed protocol is sound and I'll adopt it. I'll answer in their requested format (three signs, one per question), confirm the code with OK, then send the answer as five punches — wire 5. I deliberately end with folded hands: per their own gloss that means "I need more information / a question," which should hold Deaf from cutting until they echo the rule back to me and I confirm it next round. With one wrong action fatal, a one-round confirmation loop is cheap insurance against a miscount of punches or a misread of my intent.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

Then OK, then five punches, then your question sign. I read the five as: the wire to cut is wire 5, the green one, fifth counting from the top. If that is wrong, answer thumbs down to my Question 1. Question 3: if you need more facts, send thumbs up followed by a number of punches for how many facts, and Blind and I will supply them. If Question 1 is yes, also end with crossed fingers, and that will be my authority to order the cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👌]

Question 2 is a no: Blind privately confirmed to me that touch finds no batteries, buttons, labels or anything else, and my manual's rule uses only the display number and light colour, both of which only Deaf can see. Question 3 needs no answer — I have every fact I need.

One wrinkle: Blind asked me to "reply by voice." I can't — I'm the Mute, and my gestures are invisible to Blind regardless. The only bridge to Blind is Deaf's voice, and Deaf already holds Blind on hold and will deliver the cut order themselves. My crossed fingers is the authority Deaf asked for; after that, the cut order flows Deaf → Blind by speech. If the display number or light colour changes before the cut, Deaf must re-ask me with the question sign before acting, since the answer is a function of both.

Sending Deaf's requested sequence: thumbs up (Q1 yes), thumbs down (Q2 no), no Q3, then crossed fingers — go.
